name: La Reine Marlene - SIA Project 23 24
description:
La Reine Marlene is a company specialized in the sale of home materials
    and products. The company is redesigning its information system in order
    to improve operational efficiency and customer service.

    The system supports interactions with a large network of suppliers.
    Suppliers must register in the system by providing credentials and company
    information, including VAT number, address, and an IBAN for payments.
    Registered suppliers can submit proposals for their products by specifying
    the product category, selling price to La Reine Marlene, availability,
    photos, description, and guaranteed delivery time.

    After a product proposal has been submitted, the supplier cannot modify it
    until a response is received. The administration department is notified
    whenever a new proposal is submitted and evaluates it by choosing among
    three possible outcomes: accepted, revisions requested, or rejected.

    If a proposal is accepted, a separate order-management process starts and
    the retail price to be displayed in the store is added to the order
    information. If revisions are requested, the administration department
    must explain them in a comment. The supplier is notified and has five
    working days to modify the proposal, add response comments, and resubmit it.
    If the supplier does not modify the proposal within the deadline, the
    proposal is removed from the system and the supplier is notified.

    Administrators receive a reminder every 48 hours for proposals that are
    still waiting to be evaluated. If a proposal is not evaluated within ten
    working days, the system automatically rejects it and notifies the supplier.

    Once ordered products are shipped and arrive at one of the La Reine Marlene
    stores, the goods-receiving staff verifies each product. Since the company
    does not use warehouses, every available product is directly exposed in the
    store. Products are catalogued according to category, available quantity,
    and store location.

    During goods reception, the operator checks each delivered product. If no
    problem is found, the product is confirmed and the system proposes a list
    of possible store locations. The operator selects a location and the product
    is passed to the staff responsible for placing it in the store and printing
    the corresponding price. If a problem is detected, the operator reports it
    by adding a comment and the product is not admitted into the store.

    At the end of the receiving procedure, the order department processes the
    result. If all products have been accepted, the order is completed and the
    supplier is paid. Otherwise, the order is updated and remains open while
    waiting for a later delivery that completes it. In both cases, specific
    notifications are sent to the supplier.

    The system tracks inventory levels in real time. When a product reaches a
    predefined critical reorder threshold, the order department receives an
    automatic notification. Administrators can configure automatic reorder and
    replenishment actions for selected products.

    In case of automatic reordering, an order is sent to a predefined supplier,
    who has two working days to confirm it. If no critical threshold and
    automatic reorder rule are defined, the order department manages the new
    order through a separate process.

    Customers can purchase products either in physical stores or through the
    online store. Registered online customers can browse the digital catalogue,
    select products and quantities, and complete an order. The system
    automatically calculates the order total, including taxes and shipping costs.

    Customers can pay using Visa or Mastercard credit cards, PayPal, Satispay,
    the La Reine Marlene purchase card, or an immediate online bank transfer
    through supported banks.

    Once an online order has been paid, the system tracks the delivery in real
    time. Customers receive a link by email that allows them to follow the
    shipment status. Customers who have provided consent to use their mobile
    phone number also receive notifications when estimated delivery times are
    updated. Once the product is delivered, the order is marked as completed.

    Deliveries are performed by partner shipping companies. Each online purchase
    is randomly assigned to a shipping provider. The same online shopping
    procedures are available both through the website and through the dedicated
    application.

    The information system also provides customer support. Customers can submit
    questions, assistance requests, and complaints by opening support tickets.
    Each support ticket is automatically assigned to a customer-service agent.
    The agent is notified and has 24 hours to respond. If no response is provided
    within that time, the ticket is reassigned to another operator and service
    statistics are updated.

    When the customer receives a response, the customer is notified and has five
    working days to reply. If no reply is received within that period, the ticket
    is automatically considered closed.

    Finally, the system collects data regarding orders, sales, inventory, and
    customer support. These data are used by company management to analyze
    business performance and support strategic decision making.

highLevelGoals: The supplier aims to successfully register their company information, including VAT number, address, and IBAN, to become an authorized partner of La Reine Marlene.
The supplier seeks to efficiently submit detailed product proposals, including category, selling price, availability, photos, description, and guaranteed delivery time.
The supplier desires to receive timely notifications regarding the evaluation status of their product proposals (accepted, revisions requested, or rejected).
The supplier needs the ability to modify and resubmit proposals within a specified timeframe when revisions are requested by the administration department.
The supplier expects to receive notifications and payments for products that have been accepted and processed through the order management system.
The administrator aims to efficiently review and evaluate all submitted product proposals from suppliers.
The administrator needs to clearly communicate the outcome of proposal evaluations (accepted, revisions requested with comments, or rejected) to suppliers.
The administrator seeks to be reminded of pending proposals and ensure all proposals are evaluated within the defined timeframe to prevent automatic rejection.
The administrator desires to configure and manage automatic reorder and replenishment actions for selected products based on critical reorder thresholds.
The goods-receiving operator aims to accurately verify each delivered product against order details upon arrival at the store.
The goods-receiving operator needs to efficiently report any problems or discrepancies detected with delivered products, preventing them from being admitted into the store.
The goods-receiving operator seeks to select and assign appropriate store locations for accepted products to be displayed.
The store staff aims to efficiently place newly received products in their designated store locations and print corresponding price labels.
The order department staff aims to process the results of the goods reception procedure to update and finalize orders, ensuring accurate inventory and supplier payments.
The order department staff needs to manage new orders, including those triggered by critical reorder thresholds or through a separate manual process.
The order department staff expects to receive automatic notifications when a product's inventory level reaches a predefined critical reorder threshold.
The customer aims to easily browse the digital catalogue, select desired products and quantities, and add them to an order.
The customer seeks to complete purchases securely, either in physical stores or through the online store, using various payment methods.
The customer desires to track the real-time status of their online orders and deliveries, receiving updates via email or mobile notifications.
The customer needs to be able to submit questions, assistance requests, or complaints by opening support tickets and respond to agent replies.
The customer-service agent aims to efficiently receive, manage, and respond to customer support tickets, assistance requests, and complaints.
The customer-service agent seeks to provide responses to customer tickets within a 24-hour timeframe, ensuring prompt customer service.
Company management aims to access and utilize collected data regarding orders, sales, inventory, and customer support for business analysis.
Company management seeks to leverage business performance data to inform and support strategic decision-making processes for the company.

The system allows the administrator to trigger an automated notification to the supplier, including the comments for revisions.
The system automatically sends alerts to the administrator for proposals that are approaching their evaluation deadline.
The system provides a visual interface for the administrator to monitor the status of all proposals and their respective deadlines.
The system allows the administrator to set a minimum inventory level for a product that triggers a reorder action.
The system allows the administrator to activate the automatic reorder functionality for a selected product.
The system allows the administrator to deactivate the automatic reorder functionality for a selected product.
The system allows the administrator to update the parameters of an already configured automatic reorder rule.
The system provides a comprehensive list of all products with active or inactive automatic reorder rules and their settings.
The system allows the operator to access the expected products and quantities for a specific incoming delivery.
The system allows the operator to record the arrival of individual products by scanning barcodes or manually entering product IDs.
The system allows the operator to confirm that a received product matches the details of the corresponding order item.
The system allows the operator to log issues such as damaged items, incorrect quantities, or wrong products for a received delivery.
The system allows the operator to attach additional information, such as textual notes or images, to a reported product delivery problem.
The system allows the operator to flag a specific delivered product as unacceptable for admission into the store due to a detected issue.
The system provides a list or map of available physical locations within the store where products can be placed.
The system allows the operator to link a received and accepted product to a designated physical location within the store.
The system allows the operator to adjust the stock level of a product for a particular store location after placement.
The system provides the store staff with a list of products that have been received and are awaiting placement on the store floor.
The system allows the store staff to mark a product as physically placed in its assigned location within the store.
The system allows the store staff to initiate the generation and printing of price labels for selected products.
The system allows the order department staff to access reports detailing the outcome of product deliveries and verification.
The system allows the order department staff to modify the status of a purchase order (e.g., 'partially received', 'fully received') according to the goods reception report.
The system allows the order department staff to approve payment to a supplier once the corresponding products have been successfully received and verified.
The system allows the order department staff to manually initiate and create a new order for products.
The system allows the order department staff to examine reorder suggestions automatically generated based on inventory thresholds.
The system allows the order department staff to confirm and proceed with an automatically suggested reorder.
The system allows the order department staff to make changes to an already created purchase order.
The system allows the order department staff to cancel an existing purchase order.
The system automatically sends a notification to the order department staff when a product's stock level reaches a predefined low point.
The system provides a visual overview for the order department staff to monitor products that are at or below their critical reorder thresholds.
The system allows the customer to find products using search terms or by navigating through product categories.
The system allows the customer to access comprehensive information about a specific product, including its description, price, and photos.
The system allows the customer to select a product and a desired quantity, then place it into their virtual shopping cart.
The system allows the customer to delete a selected product from their virtual shopping cart.
The system allows the customer to change the number of units for a product already present in their shopping cart.
The system allows the customer to choose from available payment options (e.g., credit card, digital wallet) during online checkout.
The system allows the customer to securely enter and transmit their payment information (e.g., card number, expiry date) for an online purchase.
The system sends a notification or displays a message to the customer confirming that their online order and payment were successful.
The system allows the customer to begin the payment process for a purchase made in a physical store.
The system allows the customer to query and view the real-time progress of their online order's delivery.
The system automatically sends email alerts to the customer when their online order's status changes (e.g., 'shipped', 'out for delivery').
The system automatically sends mobile alerts (e.g., SMS, push notification) to the customer when their online order's status changes.
The system allows the customer to initiate a new request for assistance, question, or complaint.
The system allows the customer to access a list of all their submitted support tickets, along with their current status and past interactions.
The system allows the customer to provide further information or respond to an agent's message within an open support ticket.
The system automatically sends an alert or message to the customer when a customer-service agent has responded to their support ticket.
The system allows the agent to view all customer support requests that are currently active and awaiting resolution.
The system allows the agent to claim ownership of an unassigned support ticket for resolution.
The system allows the agent to access all information related to a selected support ticket, including customer query and history.
The system allows the agent to change the resolution status of a support ticket (e.g., 'in progress', 'resolved', 'closed').
The system allows the agent to compose and send a message in response to a customer's support ticket.
The system automatically notifies the agent when a support ticket is approaching its service level agreement (SLA) deadline for a response.
The system allows management to generate and view reports detailing sales performance over a chosen timeframe.
The system allows management to generate and view reports on current stock levels, categorized by product or product type.
The system allows management to access key performance indicators related to customer support, such as resolution time and ticket volume.
The system provides a visual dashboard displaying critical metrics related to orders, sales, inventory, and customer support.
The system allows management to create tailored reports by selecting and combining different data points from orders, sales, inventory, and customer support.
The system allows management to download collected business data in a format compatible with external analytical software.
